title: Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · jog70555-sec-0001-p1】Cervical cancer remains the fourth most common malignant tumor and the fourth leading cause of cancer‐related death among women worldwide, with approximately 660 000 new cases and 350 000 deaths annually [1]. Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is its main cause, and cervical cancer is largely preventable through vaccination and screening [2, 3, 4, 5, 6], and its burden remains concentrated in low‐ and middle‐income countries [7]. Japan is an exception among high‐income countries, with a substantial disease burden partly attributable to historically low HPV vaccination coverage [8, 9, 10].

【Introduction · jog70555-sec-0001-p2】Treatment strategies for cervical cancer continue to advance across disease stages, from less invasive surgery for early‐stage disease to increasingly effective systemic and local treatments for stage IVB or recurrent disease. In stage IVB cervical cancer, retrospective propensity score‐matched analyses, including a recent Japanese multicenter JROSG22‐1/JCOG1088S study, suggest that definitive pelvic radiotherapy, particularly when combined with brachytherapy, may prolong survival in appropriately selected patients, although prospective validation is required [11, 12]. For oligometastatic cervical cancer, stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) has been associated with excellent local control and favorable survival outcomes in selected patients [13].

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusions · jog70555-sec-0014-p1】In recent years, radiotherapy for cervical cancer, encompassing both EBRT and brachytherapy, has evolved substantially with advances in image‐guidance technologies. Looking ahead, the integration of AI‐assisted treatment, innovative approaches to overcoming anatomical constraints, and biological information into clinical practice may further transform the field, enabling radiotherapy to evolve from increasingly safe and precise treatment toward truly personalized care tailored to the characteristics of each patient and tumor.

【Advances in IGRT · jog70555-sec-0005-p3】3D‐IGRT using MVCT or CBCT enables organ position to be verified and corrected immediately before each treatment fraction. In addition, the clinical introduction of robotic couches capable of correcting patient positioning in six degrees of freedom based on image guidance has further improved setup accuracy [35]. These technological advances have provided the technical foundation for the safe and accurate implementation of IMRT in cervical cancer.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【FIGURE 1 · jog70555-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 Dose distributions of (A) a composite plan combining four‐field whole‐pelvic irradiation without central shielding and subsequent anteroposterior–posteroanterior (AP–PA) irradiation with central shielding, and (B) intensity‐modulated radiotherapy. Orange, light green, blue, and yellow represent the 100%, 95%, 90%, and 80% isodose levels, respectively.

【FIGURE 2 · jog70555-fig-0002】FIGURE 2 Dose distributions in the same patient undergoing (A) intracavitary brachytherapy (ICBT) alone and (B) intracavitary/interstitial brachytherapy (IC/IS BT). The round white structure within the uterine cavity represents the cross‐section of the tandem applicator, and two yellow arrows in panel B indicate the positions of the interstitial needles. The orange and light‐green lines represent the 150% and 100% isodose lines, respectively. The bladder and rectum are contoured in light blue and purple, respectively. Compared with ICBT alone, IC/IS BT improves target coverage without increasing the doses to the bladder and rectum.

【FIGURE 3 · jog70555-fig-0003】FIGURE 3 Bioabsorbable tissue spacer placement in a patient with para‐aortic lymph node recurrence after whole‐pelvic concurrent chemoradiotherapy for cervical cancer. The recurrent lymph node, contoured in red, was located at the superior edge of the previous irradiation field. (A) A portion of the bowel, contoured in light blue, was in close proximity to the recurrent lymph node, making it difficult to deliver an adequate dose for definitive radiotherapy without spacer placement. (B) A 15‐mm‐thick bioabsorbable tissue spacer, contoured in yellow, was placed between the recurrent lymph node and the bowel to enable definitive radiotherapy.
